study type: Secondary analysis of a cross-sectional study
exposure: Twin pregnancies with nonvertex first twin
cohort: Twin deliveries at ≥34 weeks of gestation from 21 low- and middle-income countries participating in the WHO Multicountry Survey on Maternal and Newborn Health
finding: The prelabor caesarean delivery rate among twins varied largely between countries, likely due to overuse in wealthier countries and limited access in low-income countries.
mod_finding: Prelabor caesarean delivery was associated with a lower risk of neonatal near miss compared to spontaneous vaginal delivery and a lower risk of early neonatal mortality among deliveries with nonvertex presentation of the first twin.
